title: q2-roadmap-launch-readiness-engineering-prep
summary: Internal engineering/product sync to finalize Q2 launch readiness checklist for the new routing and caching rollout. Discussed remaining infra work, performance regression testing, SLA targets, and incident playbook updates. Decided owners for benchmarks, security signoff, and rollout gating; next steps to run end-to-end perf tests and update canary policy.
topics: Incident playbook updates and on-call rotations
action_items: Tom Brooks: complete end-to-end perf harness with 95th percentile scenarios; due 2026-03-24
Priya Nair: verify KMS/HSM integration in staging and produce audit log sample; due 2026-03-22
Ethan Zhao: run KV cache + batching regression tests across 2 model variants and share results; due 2026-03-23
Maya Patel: update rollout doc with canary percentages and rollback triggers; due 2026-03-20
Diego Alvarez: finalize QA plan and smoke test checklist; due 2026-03-21
Leah Martinez: coordinate security signoff meeting with Legal and Trust; due 2026-03-25
next_steps: Run full perf benchmark on dedicated pool (Tom)
Share benchmark spreadsheet and raw logs (Ethan)
Update canary rollout policy and gating criteria (Maya)
Prepare customer-facing launch notes and support runbook (Diego)
transcript:
Header: 2026-03-17 10:00am PDT | Duration: 60 mins | Attendees: Leah, Tom, Priya, Ethan, Maya, Diego

[00:00] Leah: Okay, uh, good morning everyone. Thanks for joining — I know we squeezed this in. Agenda: launch readiness for Q2, perf, security signoff, and incident runbook updates. Quick round robin updates, then we'll go into the checklist.
[00:18] Tom: Morning. Quick status from infra: dedicated GPU pool is provisioned in us-west-2, but we're seeing some variance on tail latency with longer context lengths. Looks like the batching heuristics need a tweak.
[00:32] Priya: Yep, on SRE side we reproduced a 95th percentile spike around 1.8s for 16k seq. Might be KV cache warmup plus some kernel fallback on quantizaton paths — term might be "quantization" but the metric shows extra cpu fallback.
[00:45] Ethan: I ran a quick lab using the rwd-llama variant and saw similar. Could be the kernel selector falling back on fp16 emulation on some nodes. We'll collect node-level traces.
[00:58] Leah: OK, action there is, Tom/Ethan, get end-to-end perf harness updated and share the spreadsheet. We need 95th p, p99, and cost per token ballpark.
[01:10] Maya: On rollout policy, product wants a conservative canary: start 1% traffic, 10% after 24h if no regressions, 50% after 72h and full at 7 days. Need rollback triggers tied to p95 and error rate.
[01:28] Tom: That's fine but note dedicated pools might have cold-start variability. Suggest a warmup step and prefix caching to mitigate.
[01:36] Priya: Also KMS integration — we've got the key rotation framework in staging but need an audit sample for Compliance. I'll produce sample logs with envelope encryption metadata.
[01:48] Leah: Great. Leah: Security signoff — Legal and Trust want SOC 2 evidence plus audit logs for the rollout. Maya, you'll coordinate docs; Priya, you'll provide the logs.
[02:02] Diego: QA — we'll run e2e tests that include canary traffic patterns and failover to hosted variants. One question: do we have a fallback model that is cheaper but compatible if latency spikes?
[02:18] Ethan: Yes we have rad-small and rad-medium variants; the router can fallback when a node is over threshold, but we need to validate semantic parity. We'll add a small rerank eval to ensure correctness.
[02:32] Leah: Good, add that to the checklist. Also capture the regression tests we ran yesterday; there were some false positives in our synthetic load where the KV cache didn't have prefix hits. Need to test real traffic profiles.
[02:47] Tom: On canary metrics: p95, p99, error rate, model output similarity score, and cost per 1k tokens. We'll wire those into the dashboard and set alert thresholds.
[03:00] Maya: Timeline check: we want docs and tests done by end of next week so we can start canary the week after. Is that feasible?
[03:10] Priya: Yes, SRE can have staging audit logs by Monday and the KMS verification by Wed.
[03:18] Ethan: Perf harness results should be ready by Tuesday EOD if I can finish the node traces.
[03:26] Diego: QA plan by Thursday. We'll do smoke tests and a staged ramp.
[03:34] Leah: Okay, so recap: perf harness (Tom/Ethan), KMS/audit logs (Priya), canary policy doc (Maya), QA plan (Diego), security signoff meeting scheduled (Leah).
[03:47] Tom: Quick technical question — for the KV cache eviction policy, are we moving to LRU with weights for prefix frequency or stick with time-based TTL?
[03:58] Ethan: I prefer LRU with frequency weighting; TTL caused a lot of churn in our synthetic tests. But need to consider memory spikes.
[04:10] Priya: We'll run memory pressure tests, but SRE is ok with LRU if we have guardrails.
[04:20] Leah: Great. Anything else?
[04:24] Maya: Small note — add a line item for customer comms: what we tell customers if there's a degradation during canary. Diego, can you draft that?
[04:33] Diego: Yep, will draft an incident template and support playbook.
[04:38] Leah: Awesome. Let's set follow-up: Leah will schedule the security signoff and a 30-min perf review next Tuesday. We'll reconvene in a week for status. Thanks everyone.
[04:50] [End of recording]

Notes: transcription contains minor speaker mislabels and occasional mis-hearings (e.g., quantizaton -> quantization), some proper nouns abbreviated (rwd-llama), and timestamps are approximate. Links shared during call: perf spreadsheet (link: /sheets/q2-perf-benchmarks), rollout doc (link: /docs/canary-rollout-q2), security pack (link: /shared/security/audit-samples).
